review_notes: Independently read the current top-level proposal.json in full, functionality.md in full, both complete disposition ledgers, all four subjects pages, all three links pages, and both complete owned files in canonical and rendered form. The current top-level artifacts, rather than the older prior_result embedded in context, are the reviewed input.

All six proposed writes address owned function subjects and are supported. The two animation-purpose and two animation-state writes correctly replace guaranteed creation and action-wide duplicate suppression with cue-gated attempts whose protection lasts while the latch remains nonzero. The two ground-physics writes correctly replace an unproved increase in friction with conditional multiplication.

Foreign canonical definitions independently confirm nullable item creation, copying rather than retention of the caller's position pointer, the optional x2224_b2 recovery diversion, strict friction comparison, common airborne physics, ground/air conversion effects, and motion-table callback installation. Active Kirby table records confirm shared Pikachu/Pichu membership; the mapping does not depend on numeric enum labels.

The inferred entry names are reasonable descriptive aliases, not recovered canonical symbols. The canonical Pikachu counterparts independently support the naming convention. Rendered substitutions were not used as proof of helper semantics.

The top-level ledger appropriately defers additional claims that the older prior_result retained by narrowing their interpretation, including airborne non-interruptibility, unconditional grounded projectile emission, and TU-wide one-shot/completion claims.

Acceptance approves the six proposed writes, not promotion of unresolved baseline claims. Section layout, runtime attribute values, script-wide latch lifetime, physical collision-predicate terminology, unsupported-hat reachability, and detailed external completion/teardown behavior remain explicitly deferred.
No replacement proposal, new links, entities, merges, follow-up writes, or shared-artifact mutations are submitted.
